idiom_name: (T) -> Boolean function types; fun interface Specification<T> with SAM conversion and infix combinators
implementation_notes: Kotlin treats the rule as a function value: `typealias Spec<T> = (T) -> Boolean`, extension or infix helpers for composition, and the stdlib's filter/predicate-taking functions consume it. When the rule needs a name, a stable type in a public API, or visibility from Java, declare it as a fun interface (Kotlin 1.4+) with an infix and(other) combinator; SAM conversion lets callers still pass a lambda, so the two forms are interchangeable at call sites. Kotlin's own documentation recommends the function type (optionally behind a typealias) as the primary form and reserves fun interfaces largely for Java interop and legacy migration, which mirrors the trade-off here: function types compose freely but cannot carry members.
pitfalls: Function types are generic interfaces (Function1<T, Boolean>): primitive arguments and results are boxed, so a fun interface with a primitive signature - or an inline higher-order function - is measurably cheaper on hot paths.
Inline lambdas cannot be stored, returned or registered; a rule set that outlives the call needs a fun interface or a class, not an inline parameter.
A typealias rule is invisible to Java consumers and carries no members, so a public cross-language API should expose a fun interface.
A lambda has no equals/toString, so logging, deduplication and equality of rules require a named class.
